questions.q: Name three supporting characters from "उद्देश्य नक्षत्र" and state one distinct personality trait for each, using only the story text as evidence.
questions.a: Correct answer: (1) ओखलाल – practical/grounded (evidence: advises आइंस्टाइन to accept government job for stability); (2) फिरोज़ – loyal/emotional (evidence: accompanies आइंस्टाइन in his wanderings despite hardship); (3) मिर्ज़ा – skeptical/rationalist (evidence: questions the feasibility of आइंस्टाइन's star-chasing). A wrong answer that lists traits without textual evidence reveals the student is relying on imagination rather than close reading. A wrong answer that confuses ओखलाल with फिरोज़ shows failure to distinguish character voices.

questions.q: Explain in your own words how ओखलाल's worldview differs from आइंस्टाइन's, and why this difference is necessary for the story's conflict.
questions.a: Correct answer: ओखलाल values material security, social acceptance, and familial duty (he urges आइंस्टाइन to take the government job, saying "नौकरी मिल गयी तो जीवन सुखी हो जायगा"), while आइंस्टाइन pursues an abstract scientific ideal regardless of poverty. This clash externalizes आइंस्टाइन's internal struggle between duty and passion. A wrong answer that merely summarizes their dialogue without identifying the ideological clash shows surface-level comprehension. A wrong answer claiming they share the same goal reveals inability to detect thematic opposition.

questions.q: In the scene where फिरोज़ sells his belongings to fund आइंस्टाइन's experiment, identify the literary device used to characterize फिरोज़ and explain its effect on the reader's perception of आइंस्टाइन.
questions.a: Correct answer: The device is foil characterization through self-sacrificial action. फिरोज़'s sacrifice (selling his watch/books) highlights आइंस्टाइन's single-minded obsession and moral blindness to the cost borne by others. Steps: (1) Locate the scene (फिरोज़ giving money saying "तुम्हारे काम के लिये मैं सब कुछ दे सकता हूँ"). (2) Identify the contrast: फिरोज़ acts out of friendship; आइंस्टाइन accepts without protest. (3) Explain effect: reader sees आइंस्टाइन's greatness as morally ambiguous. A wrong answer naming "irony" or "symbolism" misidentifies the device. A wrong answer praising फिरोज़ without critiquing आइंस्टाइन misses the evaluative dimension.

questions.q: Compare the societal pressures represented by लालाजी (moneylender) and पंडितजी (priest) in the story. How do their different forms of authority constrain आइंस्टाइन's choices?
questions.a: Correct answer: लालाजी embodies economic coercion (debt, interest, threat of auction – "सूदखोरी का जाल"), while पंडितजी embodies religious/traditional coercion (caste duties, rituals, fear of ostracism – "धर्म के नाम पर बंधन"). Together they trap आइंस्टाइन in a material-spiritual vise: लालाजी demands cash repayment forcing pragmatic compromise; पंडितजी demands ritual conformity forcing social conformity. A wrong answer treating them as identical "villains" misses the distinct institutional forces (economic vs. religious) Premchand critiques. A wrong answer ignoring their dialogue fails to ground analysis in text.

questions.q: Critique the view that नक्षत्र (the star) functions merely as a plot device. Defend your position using the star's symbolic interactions with at least two supporting characters.
questions.a: Correct answer: नक्षत्र is a dynamic symbol, not a static device. For ओखलाल, it represents "पागलपन" (madness) – he says "यह तारा नहीं, तुम्हारा भ्रम है". For फिरोज़, it represents "श्रद्धा" (faith) – he gazes at it with आइंस्टाइन. For मिर्ज़ा, it represents "विज्ञान की सीमा" (limits of science) – he calculates its distance to prove impossibility. The star's meaning shifts per character, revealing their inner worlds. A wrong answer calling it "just a goal" ignores its polysemic function. A wrong answer citing only आइंस्टाइन's view neglects the supporting cast's interpretive roles.

questions.q: Write a 100-word diary entry from मिर्ज़ा's perspective on the night आइंस्टाइन declares he has "caught the star". Capture मिर्ज़ा's voice, skepticism, and hidden emotion.
questions.a: Criteria for a good answer: (1) First-person voice using मिर्ज़ा's vocabulary (scientific terms mixed with Urdu inflections). (2) Expresses doubt ("क्या वाकई पकड़ लिया?") but also grudging respect ("उसकी जिद ने तो पत्थर भी पिघला दिए"). (3) References a specific earlier event (e.g., the telescope calculation scene). (4) Ends with ambiguity about whether science or madness won. A poor answer uses modern slang, ignores मिर्ज़ा's rationalist persona, or makes him fully supportive – showing failure to inhabit the character's established mindset.
